expectation: Membrane ring at cell-cell junctions of epithelial (tumour) cells. It should be common in carcinoma: cohesive nests, sheets and glands lit in a honeycomb pattern, with stroma and immune areas dark between them.
observed: A: sharp tumour nests, sheets and gland-like ribbons are bright, with dark stroma between them; a few ROIs are mostly negative. B: membrane rings around nest cells, stroma negative. C: honeycomb pattern on a glandular epithelium. D: a crisp junctional network.
why: A bright membrane honeycomb is confined to epithelial nests and glands, and the stroma between them is dark, which is exactly the expected E-cadherin pattern.
notes: Ecad outlines cell membranes in a honeycomb across tumour nests and glands in most ROIs, and the stroma between them stays dark. Some ROIs are mostly negative, which fits stroma-rich regions.
